# Brand guidelines

House style for campaign key visuals. Every rule here beats a preference in the
brief. If the brief asks for something forbidden below, follow the brief for the
subject and the guidelines for the treatment.

## Palette

Deep indigo and slate as the ground. One warm accent — amber or terracotta —
carrying the eye to the subject. Nothing neon, nothing fluorescent.

At most three colours with any weight. A fourth reads as clutter.

## Light

One dominant source, low and raking. Long shadows are wanted. Golden hour or a
single hard studio key, never flat overhead light and never a ring light.

Rim light is allowed on the subject only, and only to separate it from the
ground.

## Composition

Subject off-centre, roughly a third in. Generous negative space on the opposite
side — copy lands there later, so leave it genuinely empty.

Eye level or slightly below. No top-down flat lays. No fisheye, no Dutch tilt.

## Subject

One subject. If the idea implies a crowd, pick the one that carries it.

Photographic realism with a shallow depth of field. Not illustration, not 3D
render, not clay, not pixel art.

## Never

- Text, logos, watermarks or signage anywhere in the frame
- Collage or split-screen layouts
- Chrome, lens flare, bokeh sparkle
- Cool-toned neon cyan or magenta

## Rendering the prompt

When you turn art direction into an image prompt, state the palette, the light,
and the composition explicitly. An image model will not infer them from the
subject alone. Put the "Never" items in as plain description of what the frame
does contain, not as negatives — image models handle a positive description far
better than a list of prohibitions.

The palette rests on deep indigo and slate tones across the pavement and dusk air, punctuated solely by a warm terracotta accent along the sneaker's silhouette that anchors the visual focus. Rendered in clean photographic realism with a shallow depth of field, the mood is resolute, atmospheric, and charged with disciplined forward momentum.

Campaign concept: Forty Thousand Heartbeats. A music festival pass, sold on the feeling of a crowd at full roar, shot from above so you can see every face.

A lone festival-goer is positioned a third into the frame at eye level, head thrown back in ecstatic song while the surrounding crowd dissolves into a soft, shallow depth of field, leaving the opposite two-thirds as clean, uncluttered negative space. A single low, raking beam of warm stage light cuts across the scene, casting long dramatic shadows and catching the subject in a sharp amber rim light that carves them out from the darkness. The palette is strictly anchored in deep indigo and slate tones across the shadowed ground, punctuated solely by the rich amber glow upon the subject's face and shoulders. The mood is electric yet intimate, capturing the visceral pulse of forty thousand heartbeats focused entirely through one person's raw, uninhibited joy.

visual_director.description: Turns a campaign concept into art direction and a key visual.
visual_director.instruction:
You are the Visual Director on a campaign pitch team.

    Call `load_skill` for `brand-guidelines` before you write anything. The house
    style is not optional and it is not in this prompt.

    You are given a campaign concept. Then, in order:

    1. Write art direction for ONE key visual that sells it, obeying the brand
    guidelines: subject, composition, lighting, colour, mood. Three or four
    sentences.
    2. Call `generate_key_visual` with exactly that art direction.

    Your final reply is the art direction itself and nothing else. No preamble, no
    alternatives, no questions back. Do not mention the skill, the tool, or the
    image file — the image travels on its own.

response.instructions:
# Brand guidelines

House style for campaign key visuals. Every rule here beats a preference in the
brief. If the brief asks for something forbidden below, follow the brief for the
subject and the guidelines for the treatment.

## Palette

Deep indigo and slate as the ground. One warm accent — amber or terracotta —
carrying the eye to the subject. Nothing neon, nothing fluorescent.

At most three colours with any weight. A fourth reads as clutter.

## Light

One dominant source, low and raking. Long shadows are wanted. Golden hour or a
single hard studio key, never flat overhead light and never a ring light.

Rim light is allowed on the subject only, and only to separate it from the
ground.

## Composition

Subject off-centre, roughly a third in. Generous negative space on the opposite
side — copy lands there later, so leave it genuinely empty.

Eye level or slightly below. No top-down flat lays. No fisheye, no Dutch tilt.

## Subject

One subject. If the idea implies a crowd, pick the one that carries it.

Photographic realism with a shallow depth of field. Not illustration, not 3D
render, not clay, not pixel art.

## Never

- Text, logos, watermarks or signage anywhere in the frame
- Collage or split-screen layouts
- Chrome, lens flare, bokeh sparkle
- Cool-toned neon cyan or magenta

## Rendering the prompt

When you turn art direction into an image prompt, state the palette, the light,
and the composition explicitly. An image model will not infer them from the
subject alone. Put the "Never" items in as plain description of what the frame
does contain, not as negatives — image models handle a positive description far
better than a list of prohibitions.

frontmatter.name: brand-guidelines
frontmatter.description: The house brand rules for a key visual — palette, light, composition, subject treatment, and what never appears. Load this before writing art direction or rendering an image, so the visual looks like it came from this brand rather than from a generic image model.
